title: FastAPI basics
text: FastAPI is a Python web framework for building APIs using standard Python type hints. It is built on Starlette for web functionality and Pydantic for data validation. FastAPI can generate OpenAPI documentation automatically.

title: FastAPI async endpoints
text: An async FastAPI endpoint is useful when the endpoint performs I/O using awaitable libraries such as an asynchronous HTTP client. Async I/O allows other requests to make progress while the application waits for network operations.

title: Pydantic validation
text: Pydantic models validate and parse untrusted input into typed Python objects. In FastAPI, request bodies can be declared with Pydantic models, which makes validation errors explicit and produces useful OpenAPI schemas.

title: Train validation test split
text: A training set is used to fit model parameters, a validation set is used for model selection and hyperparameter tuning, and a test set is held out for final unbiased evaluation. The test set should not influence model selection.

title: Precision and recall
text: Precision is the fraction of predicted positive examples that are actually positive. Recall is the fraction of actual positive examples that the model identifies. Precision-recall tradeoffs are especially important when false positives and false negatives have different costs.

title: F1 score
text: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It is useful when a single metric should balance precision and recall, particularly for imbalanced classification problems.

title: Retrieval augmented generation
text: Retrieval augmented generation, or RAG, retrieves relevant external documents before generation. The retrieved context can ground the language model and reduce the need for the model to rely on memorized knowledge.

title: RAG grounding
text: A grounded RAG system should instruct the language model to answer from retrieved context and to say when the context is insufficient. Retrieval quality, context selection, prompt design, and answer verification all affect factuality.

title: Embeddings
text: Text embeddings map text into vectors so semantically or lexically related content can be compared. Cosine similarity is commonly used to compare normalized embedding vectors. For small corpora, TF-IDF retrieval can be a simple and transparent alternative.

title: Python type hints
text: Python type hints document expected types and allow static analysis tools to detect many classes of errors before runtime. They also improve editor support and make API contracts easier to understand.

title: Dependency injection
text: Dependency injection separates object construction from business logic. In web applications it can make external clients, repositories, and configuration easier to replace in tests.

title: API key handling
text: API keys should be supplied through environment variables or a secrets manager rather than committed to source control. Logs should avoid printing credentials, authorization headers, or other sensitive values.

title: API testing
text: FastAPI applications can be tested with an ASGI HTTP client without starting a real web server. External services should normally be mocked in unit and integration tests so tests remain deterministic and inexpensive.
